content:
Michael Gray, the actor who played Billy Batson on CBS's 1970s live-action series Shazam!, has died. He was 75.

Gray died of natural causes on Friday, Oct. 16, in Palm Desert, California, his representatives told People, Variety and USA Today in a statement released Thursday, Oct. 22.

For three seasons on CBS Saturday mornings, from 1974 to 1976, Gray played the teenage boy who could transform into the superhero Captain Marvel simply by speaking the show's title word. The role made him a 1970s teen idol, with his face regularly appearing on the covers of Tiger Beat and other teen magazines.

Before Shazam!, Gray got his start on television in 1972 on NBC's The Little People alongside Brian Keith and Shelley Fabares, and in 1973 appeared as Marcia Brady's boyfriend Jeff on The Brady Bunch. Decades later, he paid homage to his roots with a cameo in 2023's Shazam! Fury of the Gods, and voiced a fictionalized version of himself on the animated series Archer.

His Shazam! co-star John Davey, who portrayed Captain Marvel, remembered Gray in a statement: "Mike was just a loving, sweet guy with a great sense of humor. He loved acting, loved doing the show and, in recent years, loved appearing at comic cons. He really enjoyed meeting and chatting with the fans. Mike was a wonderful man — I don't think he ever stopped smiling."

Rest in peace, Michael Gray.
